title: Fiesta Bowl 1996: Black Jersey Night
description: Practice-jersey pride, a Fun 'n' Gun offense on ice, and a long option dagger—Go Deep into Nebraska's title blowout.
imageHint: Desert night, black jerseys, and an option dagger down the sideline

questions.question: In the Jan. 2, 1996 Fiesta Bowl, Nebraska's defense—named for the color of its practice jerseys—helped crush Florida. What nickname is that?
questions.explanation: Only defensive starters earned the black jersey in practice. Offense wore white. The name outlived the laundry rule.

questions.question: Those Blackshirts spent the night chasing which Florida Heisman quarterback's Fun 'n' Gun attack?
questions.explanation: Steve Spurrier's offense had lit up the SEC. In the desert it threw interceptions, ate sacks, and watched the deficit become a landslide.

questions.question: While Wuerffel scrambled, which Nebraska quarterback ripped a 75-yard option touchdown that became the night's signature cut?
questions.explanation: He broke tackle after tackle down the sideline. Broadcasters ran out of verbs. The Blackshirts got the stops; Frazier got the legend clip.

questions.question: Frazier's masterpiece capped a national-title win over Florida—what was the final score?
questions.explanation: It remains one of the most lopsided title games ever. Nebraska finished 12–0. The defense that wore black on Wednesday had made Saturday look easy.

questions.question: After that title blowout over Florida, which All-American defensive end—later a Rams Super Bowl champion—stood as a face of those mid-90s Blackshirts?
questions.explanation: Two-time All-American across the mid-90s window, then a Super Bowl with St. Louis. Suh's Outland year came a generation later.

questions.question: Which defensive coordinator ran the Blackshirts from 1982 through the mid-90s title years?
In 2009, which defensive tackle—nicknamed "Baby Giraffe" in Lincoln—won the Outland and Bronko Nagurski awards?
questions.hint: Went No. 2 overall to Detroit the next spring

easterEgg.title: You earn it
easterEgg.text: In the Devaney years and after, black jerseys weren't merchandise. Defensive starters got them for practice; everyone else watched. The nickname outlived the laundry rule.
